title: Favorite recorded solos
summary: He picks 'Rifftime', 'Raid the Joint', 'Holiday for Swing' and mute playing.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Do you have any particular recorded solos of your playing that you like more than others for any reasons? And if so,
could you tell us about them?

Well, I, you know, once I hear the records cause I had something on oh, a tune that Avery Parrish composed. I'm just trying to think of the name of it. That's when I was playing high. "Rifftime", that's the name of it. "Rifftime". That's, and then another one that I did on one recorded tune which I liked, it wasn't bad, was "Raid The Joint". Sam wrote that. I'd get a chance to play downstairs a little bit then go up, playing above, you know.

Oh yeah. I had to stay high on that cause I, all the trumpet playing I done. That was all right too. But, that was just showing you mostly how high I could go, you know. Cause I was, I ended up on the Fattissimo B flat I think.
I do a little mute on that stuff.
